question: In a living poisoning case, forensic specimens (blood, urine, gastric aspirate) should ideally be collected BEFORE administering antidotes or performing gastric lavage, to preserve evidence integrity.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Pre-treatment specimens are the cleanest legal evidence and contain the highest poison concentrations. In practice, at minimum a pre-treatment blood sample should be drawn during IV line insertion — simultaneously with resuscitation, not instead of it.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Collecting specimens before antidote/lavage preserves the highest quality evidence: pre-treatment blood has the highest poison concentration; gastric contents are undiluted; urine is uncontaminated. However, this must NEVER delay life-saving resuscitation — ABCDE always first.
